answer: One workable design: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because oasis only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, orchard is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any wander approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
